name: FTK Imager

name: Guymager

name: dc3dd

name: GNU ddrescue

name: libewf and ewf-tools

name: Autopsy

name: The Sleuth Kit
developer: Brian Carrier and Sleuth Kit Labs
summary: Command-line tools and a library for examining disk images and file systems. Autopsy is built on it.

name: IPED

name: Dissect

name: TestDisk and PhotoRec

name: bulk_extractor
summary: Scans raw data without parsing file systems and extracts email addresses, URLs, card numbers and other features.

name: Foremost
developer: Jesse Kornblum, Kris Kendall and Nick Mikus
summary: A classic file carver that recovers files from images based on their headers, footers and structure.

name: Binwalk
summary: Finds and extracts files and file systems embedded inside firmware and other binary blobs.

name: Eric Zimmerman's Tools
summary: A suite of fast, precise parsers for the registry, MFT, event logs, prefetch, shellbags and more.
licence_note: Mixed: most command-line tools (for example MFTECmd, EvtxECmd, PECmd, bstrings) are open source under MIT on GitHub; some GUI tools such as Registry Explorer and Timeline Explorer are free but closed source.

name: Registry Explorer
summary: A registry hive viewer with bookmarks for forensic keys, deleted key recovery and plugins.

name: Timeline Explorer
summary: A viewer for large CSV timelines and tool output with fast filtering, grouping and search.

name: MFTECmd
summary: Parses the NTFS $MFT, $J, $LogFile and related files into CSV for timeline analysis.

name: EvtxECmd
summary: Parses Windows event logs into CSV or JSON using maps that normalise each event type.

name: PECmd
summary: Parses Windows Prefetch files to show which programs ran, when and how often.

name: RegRipper
summary: Extracts and interprets forensic data from registry hives using a large set of plugins.

name: SRUM Dump
summary: Extracts the System Resource Usage Monitor database, showing application and network usage history.

name: NirSoft utilities
summary: A large collection of small viewers for browser history, USB devices, network activity and Windows artifacts.

name: Sysinternals Suite
summary: Microsoft's utilities for inspecting processes, autoruns, handles and system activity on live Windows systems.

name: KAPE
summary: Collects key artifacts from a live system or image in minutes, then runs parsers over them. Free for many uses; paid engagements need a licence.

name: Volatility 3
summary: The standard framework for analysing RAM dumps: processes, network connections, injected code, registry hives and more.
licence_note: Source code is public under the Volatility Software License (VSL) 1.0, which is not OSI-approved.

name: MemProcFS

name: WinPmem
summary: Small command-line tool that captures physical memory from a running Windows machine.

name: LiME
summary: Loadable kernel module that dumps memory from Linux and Android devices, to disk or over the network.

name: AVML

name: Belkasoft RAM Capturer
summary: A small free utility that dumps Windows memory and can run from a USB stick.

name: Andriller CE

name: jadx

name: scrcpy

name: iLEAPP
summary: Parses logs, events and app data from iOS extractions and backups into an HTML report.

name: libimobiledevice

name: pymobiledevice3

name: UFADE

name: APOLLO

name: mac_apt

name: KnockKnock

name: UAC

name: osquery

name: Wireshark
summary: Captures and inspects network traffic packet by packet, with decoders for thousands of protocols.

name: Zeek

name: tcpdump

name: Zui

name: Security Onion
summary: A Linux platform that bundles network monitoring, log management and case tools.

name: DeepBlueCLI

name: DFIR-IRIS
